reason: Not refuted: the rider is non-negative and cheap. But its value is much smaller than claimed, and the patch as written is not fail-soft. VALUE: (a) I re-measured on x138 itself. Using the exp60 lab final graphs (56 train clips, x138 head stems excluded, official metric; scratchpad floatlab.py) I compared round and safe coordinates. Safe gives +0.00229, CI90 [+0.00061, +0.00398], 16 wins / 7 losses. Edge TP +30 and FP -71; divisions are identical. By embryo, 44b6 is +0.0019 and 6bba +0.0023. The lab effect is therefore real on the head base too. (b) The same lab size (+0.0025 on e48) tied TWICE on the LB (P32, P33). P32 exp52 already had the V1284 head's sub-voxel z, so 'what changed (1)' is not new. The per-embryo effect is homogeneous (4 of 4 embryo x base cells are about +0.002). Two ties are therefore unlikely (~0.1) if the server keeps Float64. The posterior is P(Float64 server) ~0.1-0.2 against a prior of ~0.6 from royerlab csv_to_geffs. (c) The most likely world is a server that rounds or casts. There the safe encoding is byte-equivalent: exactly 0 on public AND private, and the unrounded score is unchanged too, so 'unrounded ordering' (change 2) buys nothing there. Realistic E(private) ~ 0.13 x ~+0.001 = ~+0.0001, or ~1-3 expected ranks, not 6-25. P(harm from the metric) ~0. FEASIBILITY: (d) The port is trivial. The x138 writer's anchors (int(round()) z/y/x lines, the row_id assert) match exp39's verbatim, so the only change is cells_src[7] -> cells_src[CELL['post']] plus adding 'floatout' to the x138 patch list. (e) DEFECT: FLOATOUT_CHECK (tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.1315-1362) is a bare-assert last cell. Any assert on the hidden rerun raises 'Notebook Threw Exception', which errors the F1 file. That violates 'every stage fail-soft' (R7). The risk is low because exp52 passed the same hidden data with the same row format, but it is not zero on a different pipeline (x138 fallback/degrade paths). The check must restore an integer CSV on failure. (f) Rules: it is not in the pre-registered R3 rider list (C01/C05/C04), so it needs the user's OK. It fits R8 (port done before 27 Sep 12:00) and costs 0 runtime. Stacked on K3 it does not confound forkmid's read in the likely cast-server world. Net: keep it as a low-priority free option (below the E-list per R10), not an 'urgency today' item.
fix: Only if the user OKs it as an R3 coordinate rider, and after the higher R10 items. (1) Port: in patch_floatout use cells_src[CELL['post']]; add BASES['x138']['patches'] += ('floatout',); keep OUTPUT_FLOAT_COORDS=0 byte-identical (a builder test: an x138 K2 build with --patch floatout and mode 0 has the same cells as without it). (2) MAKE THE CHECK FAIL-SOFT: write_test_submission first saves the integer CSV text (or FLOATOUT_REF rows). The check cell wraps everything in try/except. On any failure it prints 'FLOATOUT FAILED -> integer CSV restored' and rewrites submission.csv from the integer writer (floor of every node z/y/x, or a re-run of the writer with mode 0). Add a FORCE_FAIL --lab knob and a unit test that the restored CSV sha256 == the mode-0 CSV. (3) Use safe mode only (x138 lab: safe +0.0023 > plain float +0.0016). (4) Fold the dummy gate into the S12 (or K3) dummy: 'FLOATOUT CHECK PASSED'; floor(z/y/x) == the in-kernel FLOATOUT_REF integers on 100% of node rows; no 'FLOATOUT FAILED'; node/edge rows, ids and fork counts identical after flooring. Compare with the matching mode-0 dummy CSV if one exists; otherwise rely on the builder byte-identity test. (5) F1 line only, never the exp58n twin, never a dedicated slot. R3 read: keep unless public <= previous - 0.002. Record in CONTEXT BEFORE the score that a public tie is the expected outcome (cast server) and is not evidence either way.
realistic_gain: Private ~+0.0001 expected (0 with probability ~0.85: the server rounds or casts, as P32/P33 imply; ~+0.0005..+0.002 with probability ~0.1-0.2 if it keeps Float64). Public ~0 (a tie is expected). Rank effect ~1-3 places in expectation, not 6-25. The x138 lab effect is real if the server kept floats: safe +0.0023, CI90 [+0.0006, +0.0040], 16 wins / 7 losses on 56 exp60 clips. Cost ~1.5-2 agent-h plus ~0.5 h for the fail-soft wrapper, 0 GPU and 0 runtime.
